title: a configured raw provider error is a successful match, not a fake failure
note: The inverse of every instinct about error handling. A configured non-2xx raw response is a successful match: outcome matched, error null, invocation count incremented, and verification passes (§21.1, §44.9). The distinction that matters is intentional-provider-error versus fake-server failure, and the specification keeps the two categories distinguishable (§21).

journal._timestampOmitted: timestamp is diagnostic only (§8.6, §41.7) and is not asserted

conventions.comparison: parsed JSON values; object key order and insignificant number spelling 1 versus 1.0 are not significant (§44 preamble, §39.4)
conventions.messageSentinel: the literal string <not asserted> marks a field whose value the specification does not freeze; a runner MUST skip it
